question: Who among the following is called the ‘Bhajan Samrat’ of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Anup Jalota**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Anup Jalota** is renowned as the 'Bhajan Samrat' of India for his exceptional contribution to devotional music.
 
• He has been awarded the **Padma Shri**, India's fourth highest civilian award, in 2012 for his contributions to the field of Art-Indian Classical Music - Vocal.
 
• Anup Jalota is known for his soulful renditions of devotional songs and ghazals, which have earned him a large following.
 
• He has released numerous albums featuring bhajans (devotional songs), ghazals, and other forms of light music.
 
• Jalota has also performed in various prestigious music concerts and festivals both in India and abroad.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhajan:**

 
 
• A bhajan is a type of devotional song in Indian religions, typically expressing love and devotion to a deity.
 
• Bhajans are often simple and lyrical, and they can be performed solo or in a group.
 
 
 
• **Ghazal:**
 
 
• A ghazal is a form of amatory poem or ode, originating in Arabic poetry, and is often sung in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Ghazals are typically centered around themes of love, loss, and longing.
 
 
 
• **Padma Shri:**
 
 
• Padma Shri is the fourth highest civilian award in the Republic of India.
 
• It is awarded to citizens of India in recognition of their distinguished contribution in various spheres such as Arts, Education, Industry, Literature, Science, Sports, Medicine, Social Service and Public Affairs.
 
 
 
• **Indian Classical Music:**
 
 
• Indian classical music is categorized into two major traditions: Hindustani (North Indian) and Carnatic (South Indian).
 
• It is characterized by its raga (melodic framework) and tala (rhythmic patterns).
